bottom_line: In symptomatic chronic heart failure, bisoprolol vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 0.66 [95% CI 0.54–0.81]).
implications: These results support that, in stable ambulatory NYHA III–IV chronic heart-failure patients with left-ventricular ejection fraction ≤35% receiving diuretics and ACE inhibitors, bisoprolol lowered all-cause mortality versus placebo (0.66 [95% CI 0.54–0.81]) and reduced sudden death (0.56 [0.39–0.80]). They do not establish safety/efficacy for patients with severe class IV symptoms and recent instability, as the document states results should not be extrapolated to that group.

major_points.text: Multicentre double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial in Europe with intention-to-treat analysis.
major_points.quote: In a multicentre double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial in Europe

major_points.text: Population: 2647 symptomatic patients in NYHA class III or IV with LVEF ≤35% on standard therapy including diuretics and ACE inhibitors.
major_points.quote: we enrolled 2647 symptomatic patients in New York Heart Association class III or IV, with left-ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less receiving standard therapy with diuretics and inhibitors of angiotensin-converting enzyme.

major_points.text: Intervention: bisoprolol started at 1.25 mg daily and titrated to a maximum of 10 mg per day.
major_points.quote: patients bisoprolol 1·25 mg (n=1327) or placebo (n=1320) daily, the drug being progressively increased to a maximum of 10 mg per day.
The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early after the second interim analysis due to a significant mortality benefit with bisoprolol.
major_points.quote: CIBIS-II was stopped early, after the second interim analysis, because bisoprolol showed a significant mortality benefit.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with bisoprolol than placebo (156 [11.8%] vs 228 [17.3%]) with hazard ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.54–0.81).
major_points.quote: All-cause mortality was significantly lower with bisoprolol than on placebo (156 [11·8%] vs 228 [17·3%] deaths with a hazard ratio of 0·66 (95% CI 0·54–0·81, p<0·0001).

major_points.text: Sudden death was reduced with bisoprolol vs placebo (48 [3.6%] vs 83 [6.3%]) with hazard ratio 0.56 (0.39–0.80).
major_points.quote: There were significantly fewer sudden deaths among patients on bisoprolol than in those on placebo (48 [3·6%] vs 83 [6·3%] deaths), with a hazard ratio of 0·56 (0·39–0·80, p=0·0011).

major_points.text: All-cause hospital admission was reduced with bisoprolol vs placebo (hazard ratio 0.80 [0.71–0.91]).
Permanent treatment withdrawals were similar between groups (HR 1.00 [0.82–1.22]).

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients were ambulatory, aged 18–80 years

inclusion_criteria.text: Left-ventricular ejection fraction measured within 6 weeks of randomisation of 35% or less.
inclusion_criteria.quote: had a left-ventricular ejection fraction, measured within 6 weeks of randomisation, of 35% or less.

inclusion_criteria.text: Symptoms corresponding to NYHA class III or IV (dyspnoea on exertion, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, with or without oedema, and fatigue).
inclusion_criteria.quote: Symptoms had to include dyspnoea on exertion, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, with or without oedema, and fatigue, corresponding to class III or IV of the New York Heart Association (NYHA).

inclusion_criteria.text: Diagnosis of chronic heart failure made at least 3 months previously with clinical stability during the preceding 6 weeks for heart failure or 3 months for acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients had to have a diagnosis of chronic heart failure, made at least 3 months previously, with clinical stability during the preceding 6 weeks for heart failure or 3 months for acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina.

inclusion_criteria.text: Treatment had to include a diuretic and an angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitor (other vasodilators allowed if intolerant).
inclusion_criteria.quote: Treatment had to include a diuretic and an angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitor, although we allowed other vasodilators if patients were intolerant of ACE inhibitors

exclusion_criteria.text: Myocardial infarction or unstable angina pectoris in the previous 3 months.

exclusion_criteria.quote: percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty or coronary-artery bypass graft in the previous 6 months

exclusion_criteria.quote: atrioventricular block greater than first degree without a chronically implanted pacemaker

exclusion_criteria.quote: resting heart rate of less than 60 beats per min

criticisms.text: Results should not be extrapolated to patients with severe class IV symptoms and recent instability because safety and efficacy has not been established in these patients.
criticisms.quote: Results should not, however, be extrapolated to patients with severe class IV symptoms and recent instability because safety and efficacy has not been established in these patients.

criticisms.text: The apparent anomaly by aetiology in prior CIBIS resulted from post-hoc analysis, highlighting limitations of such analyses.
criticisms.quote: This observation did, however, result from a post-hoc analysis and highlights the limitations of such analyses.

criticisms.text: Left-ventricular function was not measured sequentially in this trial.
criticisms.quote: We did not measure left-ventricular function sequentially

criticisms.text: Mean age in the trial was younger than patients seen in clinical practice, limiting information about effects in older patients.
criticisms.quote: In our trial the mean age of patients was 61 years, at least a decade younger than that of patients seen in clinical practice.
